newsitem.title: USA: Edison 1,070 MW Calif. nuke seen on-line Wed.
newsitem.headline: Edison 1,070 MW Calif. nuke seen on-line Wed.

text.p: The 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant is scheduled to restart March 26 after it developed a leak in a pump valve two days ago, a spokesman for Southern California Edison Co said Friday.
It is expected to take several days after that for the unit to ramp up to full power.

Unit 2, which has been down for refueling, maintenance and unplanned repairs since Nov 30, was preparing to go on-line when the leak, located inside the unit's contained coolant system, was discovered.
The San Onofre plant is 75 percent owned and operated by Edison, while Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co owns 20 percent and the cities of Anaheim and Riverside own 5 percent.
